summary: The synthetic field is now 0x000C0000, bits 18..19 (draw.c:612), and init_pipeline_key()'s strip at draw.c:1896-1897 masks only NV_PGRAPH_BLEND_LOGICOP_ENABLE | NV_PGRAPH_BLEND_LOGICOP = 0x0001F000. 0x000C0000 & 0x0001F000 == 0, so PSH_PAD_ALPHA_ZERO now lives in bit 18 and SURVIVES the strip: ZERO and NONE are distinguishable in the pipeline key, which is the aliasing the field exists to prevent. I COMPUTED THE FIELD EXTENT MYSELF rather than take it on report, because the original defect came from a truncated read of the same header. The mask-shaped NV_PGRAPH_BLEND_* defines are exactly six -- EQN 0x00000007 (nv2a_regs.h:364), EN (1<<3) (:380), SFACTOR 0x000000F0 (:381), DFACTOR 0x00000F00 (:397), LOGICOP_ENABLE (1<<16) (:413), LOGICOP 0x0000F000 (:414) -- everything between is an enum VALUE, and the next define at :415 is NV_PGRAPH_BLENDCOLOR, a different register. Their union is 0x0001FFFF, confirming the lane's figure. 0x000C0000 is clear of it. CLOSED BY FIX (1) ALONE, independently of fix (2).
scenario: Pass 1's scenario -- a non-eds3 device rendering all 32 `Blend surface` cases into one 128x128 surface at one address, where the pad field is the only key difference and both _Z and NONE key as 0, so the cache serves one pipeline to both -- can no longer occur. The field no longer intersects the stripped mask, so a _Z pad format and a no-pad format produce different key->regs[0] on every device where blend is baked into the pipeline.
remediation: Effective. The relocation is the fix pass 1 asked for and the QEMU_BUILD_BUG_ONs are the assertion pass 1 said the comment was substituting for. No action. One blind spot in the asserts is filed separately as N1, LOW, with no current failure scenario.
evidence: draw.c:607-610 (NV2A_VK_BLEND_PAD_ALPHA_DEFINED_BITS, built from the six macros), draw.c:612 (0x000C0000), draw.c:616-626 (the three asserts), draw.c:1896-1897 (the strip, unchanged). nv2a_regs.h:363-415 read in full, not piped through head. Union recomputed by the compiler from the macros themselves: 0x0001FFFF. My own negative control, built from the macros lifted verbatim and compiled with gcc -std=gnu11 against _Static_assert (which is what QEMU_BUILD_BUG_ON expands to, include/qemu/compiler.h:73-78): 0x00030000 REJECTED on the overlap leg and REJECTED on the key-strip leg; 0x000C0000 accepted on all three; 0x00020000 and 0x00040000 REJECTED on the width leg only; 0x00018000 and 0x0000C000 REJECTED on overlap and strip; 0x00300000 and 0xC0000000 accepted. Every leg therefore has both an accepting and a rejecting candidate, so none is a tautology. Not build-verified in the real translation unit: the desktop build is a KNOWN NAMED GAP on this host (libcurl absent, confirmed). The include chain that puts all three symbols in scope is present: draw.c:23 -> renderer.h:29 (nv2a_regs.h) and renderer.h:33 (glsl/shaders.h -> psh.h), with QEMU_BUILD_BUG_ON via qemu/osdep.h.

summary: Closed, and closed by fix (2) -- the unconditional write -- exactly as pass 1 required be verified separately. SET_MASK clears the field before OR-ing (nv2a_regs.h:27-32: `(v) &= ~(__mask); (v) |= ...`), so writing PSH_PAD_ALPHA_NONE when the gate is off forces the field to 0 whatever the raw register held. draw.c:639-642 now writes it on both arms of the gate. AND IT IS SUFFICIENT AT EVERY CONSUMPTION SITE, which is the part that makes it equivalent to pass 1's suggested consumer-side gate: pgraph_vk_effective_blend_reg() is the ONLY producer of a value carrying this field, and all three callers of pgraph_vk_blend_stamps_pad_alpha() consume its output -- draw.c:2314 (static path, from 2275), draw.c:4563 (eds3 path, from 4538), draw.c:6009 (reorder path, from e->dyn_blend set at 5472). No consumer reads the raw register. CORRECTION TO THE LANE'S OWN FRAMING, in the direction that makes fix (2) MORE important: fix (1) alone would NOT have closed H2. PGRAPH MMIO is an unmasked passthrough -- pgraph_write()'s `default:` arm at pgraph.c:1015-1020 calls pgraph_reg_w(pg, addr, val) with the guest's raw 32-bit value -- so a guest can write arbitrary bits into pg->regs_[NV_PGRAPH_BLEND], bits 18..19 included. Relocation moves the field off the guest's NAMED field; it does not move it out of guest reach. The lane's ordering (fix 2 primary, fix 1 defence in depth) is right; the reason is stronger than stated.
scenario: Pass 1's scenario -- a device with no dualSrcBlend (or the feature with maxFragmentDualSrcAttachments == 0) where a guest NV097_SET_LOGIC_OP_ENABLE sets bit 16, the predicate returns true, and the renderer programs VK_BLEND_FACTOR_SRC1_ALPHA with the feature disabled and one fragment output, aborting under VK_CHECK at vkCreateGraphicsPipelines -- can no longer occur. With the gate false the field is cleared to NONE before any predicate reads it, so pgraph_vk_blend_stamps_pad_alpha() is false on every path, and neither the SRC1 substitution nor the forced ONE/ZERO/ADD alpha equation is reachable. This holds for arbitrary guest register contents, which is what closing it by construction means.
remediation: Effective and independent of H1's. Also verified that the two fixes COMPOSE without interaction: with the field at bits 18..19 the unconditional write clobbers nothing guest-visible -- bit 16 LOGICOP_ENABLE is preserved in the effective register -- whereas an unconditional write at the OLD bits 16..17 would have closed H2 while silently erasing the guest's logic-op enable from every effective value. The pair was chosen in the right order. No action.
evidence: nv2a_regs.h:26-32 (SET_MASK clears then ORs). draw.c:628-644 (pgraph_vk_effective_blend_reg, the single producer; the gate is now a ternary feeding one unconditional SET_MASK). draw.c:646-650 (the predicate). The three consumers: draw.c:2275/2314, 4538/4563, 5472/6009. pgraph.c:879-1020 (pgraph_write; the `default:` arm stores the guest value unmasked). q->dyn_blend remains RAW and is the only value restored into pg->regs_ (set from pgraph_reg_r at draw.c:4914, 5024, 6324, 6381; restored at draw.c:5190), while e->dyn_blend is effective and is never restored -- so pass 1's claim 2 still holds at this tip and no synthetic value leaks back into a register. psh.c:3793-3797 stages the uniform from the IDENTICAL expression, so the shader and the blend state cannot disagree about which draws stamp.

summary: SET_SURFACE_FORMAT now captures old_color_format before the assignment and bumps pg->pipeline_state_gen and pg->any_reg_gen when it changes (pgraph.c:2496-2502). Pass 1 asked pass 2 to check two specific things and both hold: the bump is on the COLOUR arm, in its own `if` with its own saved value, NOT folded into the zeta comparison three lines below; and an A8R8G8B8 <-> X8R8G8B8_Z8R8G8B8 transition at one address now reaches init_pipeline_key, because BOTH early-outs pass 1 named compare pipeline_state_gen -- create_pipeline()'s at draw.c:1943-1947 and check_pipeline_dirty()'s at draw.c:1810. That is why pass 1 rejected a condition-list widening and asked for a counter: one counter satisfies both exits, a condition added to one exit does not. THE BUMP COVERS EVERY WRITE OF THE FIELD. pg->surface_shape.color_format is assigned in exactly ONE place in the entire tree (pgraph.c:2497); a grep for assignments across hw/xbox/nv2a/ returns that line and nothing else. It is also in vmstate (nv2a.c:1563), which would bypass the bump, but nv2a_post_load() sets pgraph.flush_pending (nv2a.c:1500-1506), so the load path invalidates renderer state anyway.
scenario: Pass 1's scenario -- draw into X8R8G8B8_Z8R8G8B8 at address A, SET_SURFACE_FORMAT to A8R8G8B8 at the same address/pitch/size so check_surface_compatibility reuses the binding and bind_surface is never reached, draw again, and create_pipeline takes the early return so the first draw's pipeline stays bound while the uniform is staged fresh -- can no longer occur. The counter moves, both early-outs miss, the key is rebuilt and carries the new effective blend register. I ALSO CONFIRMED THE DEFECT WAS REAL rather than inheriting pass 1's derivation, because SET_SURFACE_FORMAT calls surface_update(d, false, true, true), whose upload=false branch flushes the reorder window and the draw queue (surface.c:3538-3539) -- if that flush had reset the pipeline binding, H3 would never have bitten. It does not: it submits pending draws and clears draw_queue.active, and does not touch r->pipeline_binding or r->last_pipeline_state_gen. bind_surface (surface.c:1811-1827) is the only pipeline_state_dirty setter on the surface path and is not reached on compatible reuse.
remediation: Effective. shader_state_gen deliberately NOT bumped is CORRECT and I verified the reasoning rather than accepting it: nothing in hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/glsl/ reads surface_shape.color_format at shader generation time (every `color_format` in psh.c is a TEXTURE format from NV_PGRAPH_TEXFMT0_COLOR), PshState carries no surface colour format, the stamp at psh.c:3503 is gated only on `ps->opts.vulkan && g_dual_src_pad_supported`, and padAlphaMode is staged from upload_draw_uniforms() (draw.c:4770) on every draw as well as from the create_pipeline fall-through at draw.c:1977. So the shader text does not depend on this field and a recompile would be cost with no correctness behind it. NOTHING BROKEN BY THE any_reg_gen BUMP EITHER, which has wider reach than pipeline_state_gen and so was worth checking: its two consumers are the method fast path's sfp_ok (draw.c:3829) and try_enqueue_draw_arrays' uniforms_changed (draw.c:4869), and both fail conservative -- bail to the slow path, or re-upload uniforms. The queue is empty when the bump lands anyway (the flush precedes it), and flush_draw_queue_internal's gen save/restore bracket (draw.c:5144-5147, 5397-5401) runs entirely before the bump and cannot clobber it. The GL renderer reads neither counter -- a grep for pipeline_state_gen and any_reg_gen across hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/gl/ returns nothing -- so the bump is inert there.
evidence: pgraph.c:2465-2502 (the comment and the bump; old_color_format at 2496, the assignment at 2497, the `if` at 2499-2502, the zeta arm's own saved value and `if` immediately below). draw.c:1943-1947 and draw.c:1810 (the two exits). draw.c:1984-1990 (the fall-through that rebuilds the key and re-stamps r->last_pipeline_state_gen). surface.c:3538-3539 (the flush). surface.c:1811-1827 (bind_surface). nv2a.c:1500-1506, 1563 (vmstate and post_load). #48 REPAIR CLAIM VERIFIED: pgraph_vk_blend_reg_dst_alpha_folded (draw.c:455-540) branches on surface_color_format_dst_alpha_is_one(pg->surface_shape.color_format) at draw.c:530, so the fold's output varies with the guest colour format and entered key->regs[0], and went stale with the key. The bump repairs it. SCOPED, and this is the part the claim should carry: on an eds3 device the fold is recomputed every draw at draw.c:4538 and compared against r->dyn_state.blend, so it was never stale there. The #48 repair, like H1 and H3 themselves, lands only on the non-eds3 static path -- see N5.

summary: Answered in four parts at the site (texture.c:1361-1406), three as not-regressions and one declined. THE THREE HOLD, and I checked them against the format table AND against the upload code rather than against the argument, which is a stronger result than the lane claimed. kelvin_surface_color_format_vk_map (vk/constants.h:497-600) gives all four stamping formats guest bytes-per-pixel == host bytes-per-pixel: the 1555 pair at VK_FORMAT_A1R5G5B5_UNORM_PACK16 (2 and 2) and the 8888 pair at VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM (4 and 4). Both host layouts put the guest's pad bit exactly where the guest's X bit is -- A1R5G5B5_UNORM_PACK16's A is bit 15, which is X1R5G5B5's X; B8G8R8A8_UNORM little-endian is ARGB8888, whose A byte is X8R8G8B8's X byte. AND THE UPLOAD IS UNCONDITIONALLY A COPY FOR COLOUR SURFACES: surface.c:2576-2580 computes `no_conversion_necessary = surface->color || ...` and ASSERTS it, and the transfer is memcpy/memcpy_image (surface.c:2625-2630) with an unswizzle that permutes pixel positions, not channels. No alpha is synthesised anywhere on that path. So the guest's pad byte is our image's pad byte, and #48's constant was overriding correct data. The NV062 blit patches guest memory and inherits this. The unauthored-pooled-region argument is also right and is the weakest of the three only in the sense that it concedes the pixel was never defined. CROSS-TABLE INVARIANT HOLDS: exactly four rows carry a sampled_pad_alpha override (constants.h:517 ZERO, :543 ONE, :571 ZERO, :597 ONE) and exactly four cases return non-NONE in pgraph_glsl_surface_pad_alpha_mode (psh.c:236-248), the same four, with X1A7R8G8B8_{Z,O} correctly in neither -- so the KEEP IN SYNC note at psh.c:205-211 is satisfied.
scenario: The residual scenario is the declined one and it survives, by design: a title renders into a pad-format surface, clears NV_PGRAPH_CONTROL_0_ALPHA_WRITE_ENABLE for a second pass over part of it, then samples the surface as a texture. On the masked pixels the raster does not write the pad byte, so the sampled alpha is whatever was there rather than the format's constant. Under the model this change establishes -- the pad bits are stored bytes, written by whatever writes the surface, and read back plainly -- 'whatever was there' is the byte a clear or an upload legitimately put there, so the case is narrower than it sounds; but it is a real difference from shipped behaviour and it is not fixed.
decision: THE DECLINE IS ACCEPTED. Quoted: 'Whether silicon masks the pad bits with the ALPHA write mask at all is UNMEASURED -- the pad bits are not an alpha channel, so there is a real question there and no golden in the corpus separates the two answers. Forcing the mask on for pad formats would make the stamp unconditional and is deliberately NOT done, because it would be an unmeasured behaviour change riding along with a measured one, which is the mistake blend_factor_with_dst_alpha_one() declines to make two files over.' I accept it for three reasons, and I TESTED THE PREMISE rather than accept it, because 'no golden separates the answers' is a claim of the same kind as a blocker. (1) The premise holds to the resolution my instrument has: the corpus's two write-mask suites are Color_mask_blend (one test, C00010101_O32774_S772_D0) and Color_Zeta_Disable (one test, MaskOff_ZB), neither naming a surface format, while every pad-format capture -- Clear's SCF_/SFC_ rows, Surface_format's Fmt_ rows, Blend_surface's 32 -- masks no alpha writes. No capture combines pad-format surface x alpha-write-masked draw x sample-back. (2) The alternative overrides the write mask the GUEST asked for, on a path with no oracle, which is strictly worse than leaving a known bound if silicon honours the mask and no better than a coin flip otherwise. (3) It is recorded as a bound at the site rather than as silence, which is what AGENTS.md asks of a declined finding. WHAT MY INSTRUMENT CANNOT SEE, stated so the acceptance is not read as more than it is: this is a survey of test NAMES and score rows, not of the nxdk_pgraph_tests sources. It cannot see a test that masks alpha writes without saying so in its name. If the decline is ever to become a measurement, the cheap route is to read Color_mask_blend's source for the surface format it targets, and if it is A8R8G8B8, to ask for one new disc test rather than to guess.
remediation: No action on the three answered parts. The declined part should stay declined and stay written down. If it is ever promoted, promote it as a disc test, not as a code change: one capture rendering to X8R8G8B8_Z8R8G8B8 with the alpha write mask clear and sampling back separates the two answers outright, and the fix then follows from the measurement instead of preceding it.
evidence: texture.c:1327-1410 (surface_sampled_pad_alpha and the four-part comment; the withdrawal at 1407-1409). vk/constants.h:424-476 (the SurfaceFormatInfo field comment), :485-494 (guest bytes per pixel), :497-600 (the four stamping rows with their host formats and overrides). surface.c:2565-2630 (no_conversion_necessary, asserted; the memcpy). psh.c:236-248 (the pad mode switch, four cases). docs/testing/run-2026-09-07-full-scores.tsv (the 102-suite inventory, from which Color_mask_blend and Color_Zeta_Disable are the only write-mask suites) and run-2026-09-10-clear-adreno.tsv (the current disc's SCF_/SFC_ rows, dated after the 09-07 baseline per MEMORY.md's golden-dating rule).

summary: The re-registration is correct AT THE FOLD CANDIDATE and wrong at the integration tip, and the reason is the mechanism the lane itself documented. At f0f4ab0c39 both refs are ancestors: `merge-base --is-ancestor 0e919fe51e f0f4ab0c39` and `--is-ancestor 832557813c f0f4ab0c39` both succeed. So the answer to 'does it still hold' is YES on the branch. BUT AT THE CURRENT INTEGRATION TIP 52600e6417 IT DOES NOT: `merge-base --is-ancestor 832557813c 52600e6417` FAILS. The prediction's own commit has already been landed on claude/es-de-launcher-disc-error-ojnl14 as fb43bf4bdc -- one file, 36 lines, docs only, same subject as f0f4ab0c39 -- while the five code commits have not. The mainline therefore carries a bound registration whose b_ref names code the mainline does not contain. This is the THIRD instance of M2's shape on this one issue: first an abandoned branch, then a routine rebase, now a docs commit folded ahead of its code.
scenario: The branch base 0e919fe51e is three commits behind 52600e6417, so the fold must rebase or merge. A rebase rewrites 832557813c, and the prediction sitting on the mainline then names a sha that is an ancestor of nothing -- the exact state AGENTS.md:2100-2130 was written to prevent, in the variant that is easiest to miss because the prediction file itself never changes and no gate reads it. Concretely: the hold lifts, someone reads the board (52600e6417's own subject says the HIGHs are remediated), queues an arm from the mainline's prediction, and the dispatcher resolves b_ref 832557813c -- still reachable from origin/claude/padwrite59-dualsrc-tip -- and builds it. Today that would build the RIGHT code, which is why this is MEDIUM rather than HIGH. After the fold's rebase it either fails to build (loud, fine) or, if the lane branch is still around, produces a verdict for a tree that is not the fold. NOTHING ENFORCES THE RULE: check_cited_commits.py scans nv2a_issues.toml, not docs/testing/predictions/*.json, and no other script reads a prediction's a_ref/b_ref for ancestry. AGENTS.md:2124-2128 asks for exactly that queue-time gate and it does not exist. Mitigating: no v2 request is queued -- dispatch/queue/ holds six skew44 requests and both padwrite59 arms are in queue/withdrawn/ with a README -- so nothing resolves the ref today.
remediation: Re-register AFTER the fold's rebase, not before, and treat the already-landed fb43bf4bdc as a registration that must be superseded rather than one that is satisfied. Two concrete asks. (1) At fold time, recompute both refs against the folded shas and commit the updated prediction in the SAME fold, so the mainline never carries a registration ahead of its code. (2) Build the queue-time gate AGENTS.md:2124-2128 already specifies -- refuse a request whose b_ref is not an ancestor of a live branch tip. Three occurrences on one issue is the point at which the discipline has been shown not to hold, and the project's own rule about routing applies: the record is not the delivery. One smaller note, not worth its own row: the prediction's prose says 'arm B is the tip' and 'This file is therefore the final commit on the branch', but b_ref 832557813c is the PARENT of the tip f0f4ab0c39. The choice is right -- the tip is docs-only, and naming a sha that does not exist yet is impossible -- so the sentence is false as written while the ref is correct. Fix the sentence when re-registering.
evidence: merge-base --is-ancestor 0e919fe51e f0f4ab0c39 -> 0; --is-ancestor 832557813c f0f4ab0c39 -> 0; --is-ancestor 832557813c 52600e6417 -> non-zero. git log --oneline 0e919fe51e..52600e6417 -> 9ebb1c6d33, fb43bf4bdc, 52600e6417; git show --stat fb43bf4bdc -> one file, docs/testing/predictions/issue59-dual-source-pad-write-v2.json, +36. The prediction's own text at 52600e6417 still reads a_ref 0e919fe51e / b_ref 832557813c. AGENTS.md:2100-2130. docs/testing/check_cited_commits.py (tracker only, by its own docstring). dispatch/queue/ and dispatch/queue/withdrawn/. THE LEGS THEMSELVES ARE SOUND and I checked the one that is easiest to make inert: the FAILS IF clause names the literal string 'vk dualSrcBlend: enabled', and instance.c:998-1007 sets verdict to exactly "enabled" on success, so the logcat line reads 'vk dualSrcBlend: enabled (maxFragmentDualSrcAttachments=N, #59)' and the substring matches. The two failure verdicts, 'available but limit 0, NOT enabled' and 'missing, NOT enabled', do NOT contain that substring, because they differ immediately after the colon -- so the check discriminates rather than passing on any outcome.

summary: The three build asserts are not tautologies -- my own negative control reproduces the lane's, and every leg has both an accepting and a rejecting candidate -- but the set has two blind spots relative to its own stated purpose, which is that 'the next field added to that register cannot silently re-collide'. (1) A NON-CONTIGUOUS mask passes all three legs. 0x00140000 (bits 18 and 20) is accepted on overlap, on key-strip, and on width -- the width leg divides by the lowest set bit, so a mask with a hole reports width 5 and clears the `PSH_PAD_ALPHA_ONE > 3` threshold. SET_MASK would then compute (2 << 18) & 0x00140000 == 0, so PSH_PAD_ALPHA_ONE would silently read back as PSH_PAD_ALPHA_NONE and the _O formats would stop stamping. (2) The width leg is bounded by PSH_PAD_ALPHA_ONE spelled literally, so it checks the CURRENT maximum enumerator rather than the enum's maximum. A fourth PshPadAlphaMode added above ONE makes the leg pass while the field is too narrow.
scenario: No failure scenario in the shipped code -- 0x000C0000 is contiguous and PSH_PAD_ALPHA_ONE is the largest of the three modes -- SO THIS IS AN OPINION ABOUT THE GUARD AND IS RECORDED AS LOW. It is not zero, though, because these asserts exist specifically to catch a FUTURE edit, and the two edits they would miss are the two most likely ones: moving the field again into whatever bits happen to be free (which may not be adjacent) and adding a pad mode. The class the lane says it removed -- trusting a read of a header -- is removed. The narrower class of a mask that is clear of every field and still cannot hold its values is not.
remediation: Two one-line additions, if the owner wants the guard to match its stated job. Contiguity: assert that (NV2A_VK_BLEND_PAD_ALPHA >> ctz) + 1 is a power of two, or equivalently that m & (m + lowbit(m)) == 0 for m = the shifted mask. Enum bound: give PshPadAlphaMode a PSH_PAD_ALPHA_COUNT terminator and assert against COUNT - 1 instead of against ONE, so adding a mode moves the bound automatically. Neither is urgent and neither should hold the fold; both belong with whoever next touches the field.
evidence: draw.c:616-626 (the three asserts). My negative control, gcc -std=gnu11 with the macros lifted verbatim from nv2a_regs.h:364-414 and psh.h:144-148 and QEMU_BUILD_BUG_ON expanded as include/qemu/compiler.h:73-78 defines it. Results, accept/REJECT per leg (overlap, key-strip, width): 0x000C0000 accept/accept/accept; 0x00030000 REJECT/REJECT/accept (the shipped bug, rejected on two legs, reproducing the lane's control exactly); 0x00020000 accept/accept/REJECT; 0x00040000 accept/accept/REJECT; 0x00018000 REJECT/REJECT/accept; 0x0000C000 REJECT/REJECT/accept; 0x00300000 accept/accept/accept; 0xC0000000 accept/accept/accept; and the blind spot, 0x00140000 accept/accept/accept. nv2a_regs.h:26-32 (SET_MASK's `((__val) << ctz32(__mask)) & (__mask)`, which is where a hole loses the value). psh.h:144-148 (the enum, ending at ONE = 2).

summary: The paragraph rewritten to fix L2's wrong rationale still contains a wrong clause, and it is wrong in the same way: draw.c:682-684 says 'For an _O surface As is stamped to 1 and Ad is folded to 1 by surface_color_format_dst_alpha_is_one(), so min(1, 0) = 0.' That function and blend_factor_with_dst_alpha_one() rewrite blend factor ENUMS -- DST_ALPHA -> ONE and ONE_MINUS_DST_ALPHA -> ZERO (draw.c:304-323) -- and cannot change the Ad that VK_BLEND_FACTOR_SRC_ALPHA_SATURATE reads, which is the attachment's actual alpha. The conclusion is right for a different reason: Ad is 1 because the stamp or the clear stored 1 in the pad byte, not because a factor was folded. Also missing: pass 1 asked for one sentence naming the residual -- an _O surface whose destination alpha came from neither the raster nor the clear has Ad != 1, so min(1, 1-Ad) != 0 -- and noted it is worth saying because it is the case M1's declined part leaves open. The rewritten paragraph does not say it.
scenario: No failure scenario: the code is right, the arithmetic reaches the right answer, and the residual is unreachable in the corpus (the paragraph itself now says the saturate class is empty there). SO THIS IS AN OPINION AND IS DOWNGRADED. It is recorded because AGENTS.md's own note is that a wrong comment is not neutral but believed, because audit pass 1's M3 was overstated on the strength of a stale sentence in this same file family, and because this is the SECOND pass over this one paragraph -- a rationale that has now been wrong twice about the same mechanism is worth getting right rather than closing.
remediation: Two sentences, no code change. Attribute Ad = 1 to the stored pad byte rather than to the factor fold, and add the residual pass 1 asked for, cross-referenced to the declined half of M1 at texture.c:1392-1406 so the two bounds are one bound read twice rather than two.
evidence: draw.c:672-692 (the rewritten paragraph; the wrong clause at 682-684). draw.c:304-323 (blend_factor_with_dst_alpha_one: cases for DST_ALPHA and ONE_MINUS_DST_ALPHA only, `default: return factor`, so SRC_ALPHA_SATURATE passes through untouched). draw.c:288-302 (surface_color_format_dst_alpha_is_one, a predicate over the format enum). docs/audits/2026-09-18-padwrite-pass1.md, L2's remediation text, which names the residual explicitly.

summary: M1's answered parts lean on one measurement that does not support them as directly as claimed. texture.c:1370-1375 says the upload-is-exact argument is 'the same thing Clear/SFC_X1R5G5B5_Z1R5G5B5 measures on 49,104 px, where our green channel already carries the exact bytes the golden's alpha wants and only this override was zeroing them'. But that capture reads a 1555 surface through an 8888 view -- two 1555 words per 8888 texel, which is precisely why the issue's own decomposition puts the pad bit in the GREEN channel and why the prediction's W2 leg has to argue from band uniformity that golden G == golden A. Its 'alpha' channel is the pad bit of an adjacent pixel, not the surface's alpha. So it is evidence that our memory holds the right bytes, which is real and useful, but it is not a measurement of the upload path's fidelity and the sentence reads as though it were.
scenario: No failure scenario -- the conclusion is independently true. I verified the upload-is-exact claim from the format table (guest bpp == host bpp and the pad bit lands in the host alpha position for all four stamping formats) and from surface.c's asserted no_conversion_necessary memcpy, neither of which depends on that capture. SO THIS IS AN OPINION ABOUT THE CITED EVIDENCE AND IS DOWNGRADED. It is recorded because the same capture is the prediction's W2 leg and its 48-vs-0 absolute, so a reader who takes the comment at face value will also over-trust the leg; and because a 1555-through-8888 misread is itself a known defect in this area, which pass 1 cited as the reason keeping the swizzle for 1555 would have been wrong.
remediation: Reword to cite what the capture shows -- that the pad bytes in our memory match the golden's, read through a view that pairs two words -- and cite the format table and surface.c's memcpy for the upload claim, which is where it actually rests. No code change.
evidence: texture.c:1361-1378 (the upload-is-exact bullet and the 49,104 px citation). docs/testing/nv2a_issues.toml [issue.59]: 'Green is the byte a 1555 word's bit 15 lands in when two words are read as one 8888 texel'. docs/testing/predictions/issue59-dual-source-pad-write-v2.json, W2, which derives golden G == golden A from within-band uniformity rather than from the channels being the same thing. vk/constants.h:485-494 and :497-600 plus surface.c:2565-2630, which are the evidence that does carry the claim.

summary: The regenerated index's self-description names a commit that is not an ancestor of the tree it describes. provenance.emulator_commit at 832557813c is caf13a94a8, which is the PRE-REBASE sha of 'nv2a: set the dual-source shader gate after the device exists (#59)' -- the branch's own copy of that commit is e2edb6fe3c -- so `merge-base --is-ancestor caf13a94a8 f0f4ab0c39` fails. It is the stamp an index build takes from HEAD while the changes it is indexing are still unstaged. THE CONTENT IS CORRECT AND I CHECKED IT RATHER THAN INFER IT: the index stores each site's source line text alongside its file:line, so it can be validated against a tree without rebuilding. All 2,914 recorded locations match the fold candidate's own sources exactly, including 1,194 in pgraph/pgraph.c and 408 in vk/draw.c -- the two files whose line numbers the remediation shifted. Zero mismatches in 31 files. PRE-EXISTING, NOT INTRODUCED HERE: the branch base 0e919fe51e carries the same defect, stamp fef3e65f9a, also not an ancestor of itself's branch.
scenario: A reader or a gate that validates the index the honest way -- check whether the commit it claims to describe is on the branch -- gets 'not an ancestor' and concludes the index is stale when it is not. That is a false alarm, and the more dangerous inverse is available too: a genuinely stale index whose stamp happens to resolve to a live ancestor reads as fresh. Either way the stamp cannot answer the question it looks like it answers. This is the stale-artifact-measures-beautifully shape with the sign flipped, and no behaviour depends on it, so it is LOW and is really an observation about the tooling rather than a finding against this lane.
remediation: Stamp the tree, not HEAD: record the index's own input as a hash of the scanned sources, or write the stamp from `git stash create`/`git write-tree` rather than `rev-parse HEAD`, so a regeneration over a dirty tree cannot claim a commit it does not describe. Cheaper interim: have nv2a_index.py check validate recorded line text against the working tree, which is what I did here and which needs no tests checkout at all -- it would turn the stamp from load-bearing into decoration. Belongs with the index tooling's owner, not with #59, and should not hold the fold.
evidence: 832557813c's nv2a_index.json provenance.emulator_commit = caf13a94a8c4ed656c2b4cb0fbb3d5865b6fdfc4, whose subject is 'nv2a: set the dual-source shader gate after the device exists (#59)' while the branch's copy of that commit is e2edb6fe3c; merge-base --is-ancestor caf13a94a8 f0f4ab0c39 -> non-zero. Site counts 2819 at 0e919fe51e and e2edb6fe3c, 2833 at 832557813c, so it genuinely was rebuilt over the remediation's sources. Validation: every entry of idx['sites'] compared, loc by loc, against `git archive f0f4ab0c39 hw` -- 2,914 of 2,914 lines matched their recorded text. The nv2a index PREFLIGHT gate (preflight.sh:115-127) was NOT run here: it needs the nxdk_pgraph_tests checkout at the branch's own tree, and my worktree is at the integration tip, which does not contain the code commits.

summary: THE LANE'S LIMITATION IS TRUE AS STATED AND MIS-ATTRIBUTED, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS MORE THAN THE FINDING. Verified first: with eds3 blend enabled, H1 and H3 are structurally unobservable. init_pipeline_key sets `key->regs[0] = 0` under `if (r->eds3_blend_supported)` (draw.c:1900-1907), so the whole blend register including the pad field leaves the pipeline key; and create_pipeline's `use_eds3_blend` (draw.c:2065-2067) skips the entire static blend branch at draw.c:2261-2330, which is the only place the static path reads the effective register or applies the pad substitution. Blend enable, equation and write mask become dynamic states set per draw. So an arm on an eds3 part can confirm the accuracy claim and cannot confirm H1's remediation, H3's, or H3's #48 repair. BUT THE CAUSE IS A BUILD FLAG, NOT THE HARDWARE. OPT_DYNAMIC_BLEND is `#define`d to 1 at vk/renderer.h:50, and every one of the four things that make the static path dead is inside `#if OPT_DYNAMIC_BLEND`: the eds3 feature-enable block (instance.c:915-943), the key zeroing (draw.c:1899-1908), the eds3 draw path (draw.c:4533-4589) and the reorder path's copy (draw.c:5982-6032); `use_eds3_blend` has an explicit `#else bool use_eds3_blend = false;` arm; and instance.c:1187 already guards the dynamic-state registration with `OPT_DYNAMIC_BLEND && r->eds3_blend_supported`. So flipping that one line to 0 makes the static pipeline path LIVE on the fleet's own Adreno part. 'This fleet is a poor detector of H1 and H3' is true of the DEFAULT BUILD and not of the fleet.
scenario: The consequence of leaving it as written: H1's and H3's remediations fold on a reading alone, with pass 1 and pass 2 as their only evidence, exactly as the original findings had -- and the campaign records a limitation as a hardware fact when it is a one-line build choice. That is the blocker-is-a-claim shape: an 'unverifiable' that was not tested before being accepted. It is LOW because nothing is incorrect in the shipped code and the arm as bound is still sound; the cost is an evidence gap that need not exist.
remediation: Register a second arm, offline and now, with `OPT_DYNAMIC_BLEND 0` as its only difference from arm B, and bind it to the captures H1 and H3 actually reach: the pad-format rows of Blend_surface (one surface, one address, only SET_SURFACE_FORMAT changing, which is H1's and H3's exact shape) and Surface_format's Fmt_X* rows. Arm A of that pair is the same build at the pre-remediation code, where H1 and H3 are live -- so it is a falsifier whose A side is expected to FAIL, which is the shape MEMORY.md's tautological-falsifier note asks for. TWO CAVEATS, stated rather than glossed. (1) OPT_DYNAMIC_BLEND 0 is a build configuration nobody in this campaign has run; it needs a smoke boot before it is an arm, not a claim that it works. My check is structural -- all four eds3 sites and the feature-enable are inside the guard, and no vkCmdSetColorBlend*EXT or vkCmdSetColorWriteMaskEXT call exists outside it -- which establishes self-consistency, not that it boots. (2) It cannot run while the fleet is held, and nothing here asks for it to. Register it and leave it bound, which is what the hold's own offline order says to do. Separately: r->eds3_blend_supported being true on the Adreno part is asserted by a code comment (draw.c:4535-4537) and by instance.c:497 plus the three-feature check at 927-941; unlike dualSrcBlend, no logged boot line in this tree names it. Worth one log line next to the dualSrcBlend one, for the same reason that one existed.
evidence: vk/renderer.h:49-50 (OPT_DYNAMIC_STATES 1, OPT_DYNAMIC_BLEND 1). draw.c:1899-1908 (`#if OPT_DYNAMIC_BLEND` / `if (r->eds3_blend_supported) { key->regs[0] = 0; ... }`). draw.c:2064-2068 (use_eds3_blend with its #else false arm). draw.c:2256-2330 (the static blend branch, entered only when use_eds3_blend is false; the effective register at 2275 and the pad substitution at 2314). draw.c:4533-4589 and 5982-6032 (both eds3 command sites, both inside the guard). instance.c:915-943 (the feature enable, inside the guard), instance.c:497 (the extension), instance.c:1187. A grep for vkCmdSetColorBlend/vkCmdSetColorWriteMask over draw.c returns exactly those two sites. docs/testing/predictions/issue59-dual-source-pad-write-v2.json, FAILS IF, which is where the lane wrote the limitation.
